On April 7, 2015, following an extensive investigation by FINRA's Department of Market 
Regulation into trading activities spanning from January 1, 2010, to March 16, 2012, the Nasdaq 
Review Council accepted a Letter of Acceptance, Waiver and Consent (AWC No. 
20100243866-01).1 The regulatory document detailed a massive, multi-year scheme executed 
by Bleich’s firm to purposefully circumvent federal short-selling regulations to generate 
immense proprietary profits.1 The action resulted in a formal censure and a $3,000,000 
financial penalty, which Bleich personally signed and accepted on behalf of the firm.1 
The Mathematics of Leveraged ETFs and Beta Slippage 
To fully comprehend the severity of the regulatory breach, it is necessary to perform a deep 
examination of the specific financial instruments Bleich targeted.1 Scout Trading engaged in a 
cyclical, systemic, and highly lucrative "naked" redemption and short sale strategy.1 The 
regulatory filings explicitly list 14 specific ETFs that were the subject of the review, primarily 
highly volatile Direxion and ProShares funds.1
